fit: within-Parkinson drooling ranges and salivary flow
assessment: The 42 versus 59 contrast has inconclusive flow differences. The ordinal saliva item and resting flow have a small positive correlation. Treat the published 101-patient case–control comparison as likely overlapping.

fit: perceived versus measured swallowing and airway outcomes
assessment: In 31 participants with Parkinson disease and dysphagia, physiological test outcomes and perceived swallowing were measured separately. Drooling was clinical background.
A four-item upper gastrointestinal composite includes sialorrhea. The analysis does not break out a food-dependent drooling response.

fit: Arabic GIDS-PD and separate saliva item
assessment: The Arabic domain correlates with a salivation item. The tested constructs are clinical measurements with no separate dietary response.
Drooling was associated with male gender in the adjusted registry analysis. The geographic cohort does not report a fig comparison.

fit: saliva item and prediction of therapy initiation
assessment: The reported HR and interval apply to future medication initiation, without a measured drooling intervention.

fit: participant reports on food preparation and gum
assessment: Several participants recalled worse drooling around food preparation, while some described perceived easing with gum. No ingredient was assigned and the reports do not isolate raw fig.

fit: year-one patient-rated drooling and clinician-rated swallowing
assessment: In 73 people, changes in patient-reported drooling and assessed swallowing were inconclusive. Exact overlap with the earlier reports remains open.
